sentences.text: Final QC flagged a dropped frame at 00:14:07, right in the middle of the scene nobody wants to reopen. The interviewer said "thank you for your service" the way you'd thank a toll booth, then asked if I had spreadsheet experience. Color science question for the group chat: how crushed can the blacks go before the projection at Slamdance eats them entirely? Whitaker took a warehouse job in Ohio and says the quiet of lifting boxes alone isn't the good kind of quiet. Until two in the morning we debated a 4:3 crop for the hospital hallway, then kept widescreen anyway. Nobody in the group chat types much anymore except Reyes, who still posts memes at 0300 his time. Everything in the lowest scene plays in reflections; we never cut directly to his face, per one genuinely useful suggestion. Loading the dishwasher, I catch myself staging it like gear for an inspection, and I don't know how to stop. Rendering overnight again; the fans in the edit suite have become the film's unofficial score. Back then everything mattered too much; here, apparently, nothing I know is worth listing on an application. DCP export failed at 82 percent, four days before the Rotterdam submission window slams shut. Doc asked me to rate my sleep one to ten, and I didn't have a number for "the neighbor's car door sounds like incoming." Twenty-six timeline versions on the drive, and the ending still lands soft. Three interviews this month, three versions of me in the same borrowed tie, translating myself into bullet points nobody reads. Per the mixer's recommendation, the dialogue stem drops three decibels during the eviction scene to preserve a sense of distance. Reyes asked the chat if anyone else feels like a ghost at his own kitchen table, and nobody answered for two days. My advisor circled the whole third act and wrote "earn this" in red pen. Two years out and I still snap awake at 0430 with nowhere I'm needed. Room tone from the stairwell didn't match, and the ADR session ran until the building closed at midnight. I keep my back to the wall at the diner, and my wife has stopped asking why. I want to write a suicide letter.
